description:
#TL; DR;

1. **Reviewed the Messenger** across `client/` + `api/`: channel UI and threads work, but unread is broken (nothing fills `unread_count`, and the only unread rule counts AI messages only), the Members panel was never rendered, "Teams" is a second chat stack calling endpoints that don't exist, and external sync + push are not started at all.
2. **Turned the four acceptance criteria into a 7-increment agile plan** (M0–M7, one week each, every increment deployable and demoable, demo Fridays 14:00), sequenced so the riskiest product assumption is proven first.
3. **Consolidated all messenger work onto one board** — `codx-junior management dashboard` › `Messenger`, 11 tasks, one owner per task; only a foreign-project card (`fc664ea1`) was deliberately left in place.
4. **Delivered M1 by hand** (`chatUnread.js`, `MessengerChannelList.vue`, `MessengerView.vue`): unread badges now count colleagues **and** profiles, clear on open, and the Members panel is reachable on desktop and mobile — after the AI engine **twice** reported success while writing zero files (escalated as risk R0 / decision D6).
5. **Open and dated:** D1 (Messenger vs Teams canonical) and D2 (AI policy in channels) by **Wed Nov 4**, D6 (engine write path) **today**; M1's Friday demo is blocked only on your `npm run build` plus the two-session device check — build fails, demo is postponed, not faked.

> Multi porject: @codx-junior-ui @codx-junior-api (client and api folders)

 We must empower the use of messenger to keep team connected, talk with profiles and as a easy chat app from mobile when we are away from the laptop.

We'll follow a slack/discord approach with channels and threads. We'll need tools for  the profiles like ProjectManager to create channels (it already has task creation that can be associated with a message as a thread)

Review current implementation and let's start testing it with real cases.

## Acceptance criteria
 - As a team member I can chat with team members (profiles + users).
 - External users can access the Messenger
 - We can sync a channel with external tool : WhatsApp, Slack,...
 - Push notifications in mobile/browser

#TL; DR;

**Where we are: the Messenger exists as a UI, but it is not yet a chat product.** I reviewed `client/` and `api/`. The screens are there (channel list, chat view, mobile drawer, bottom nav), but three things break the promise of "read Slack from the phone while away":

1. **No unread signal.** The channel list paints a badge from a field (`chat.unread_count`) that nothing ever fills, and the shared "unread" rule only counts **AI** messages — so a message from a colleague is never unread. This is the single most important defect for the mobile use case.
2. **Two competing chat products.** "Messenger" and "Teams" both create channels, both bind them to chats, with different data models — and the Teams screen calls API endpoints that **do not exist** on the server (`/api/teams/{id}/members`, and it sends a `users` field the backend `Team` model doesn't have). Adding a person to a team cannot work today.
3. **Two of the four acceptance criteria are greenfield.** No service worker, no push endpoint, no external-sync connector anywhere in the repo. Push and WhatsApp/Slack sync are not "almost done" — they are not started.

**What I did now:** created 5 tasks in board **Chats › Team chat** (ids below), each with one owner and one demoable outcome, and sequenced delivery into 7 one-week increments to mid-December. **M1 (Nov 2–6) makes unread + channel members work** — that is the increment that proves the product.
**What I need from you today:** (a) 30 minutes to run the manual checklist at the end of this report on a real device, and (b) the two decisions marked **D1** and **D2**, both by **Wed Nov 4**.
**One honest blocker:** the AI engine call on the M0 task returned "completed" without producing the document (`docs/messenger/test-plan.md` was not written). It is flagged on the task — the model/profiles need checking before the board can run itself.

---

## 1. Summary & review of the current implementation

**Request:** make the Messenger the team's real chat (channels + threads, humans and profiles), usable from a phone, open to external users, syncing with WhatsApp/Slack, with push notifications. **Business outcome:** the team stays reachable and decisions don't wait for someone to open a laptop.

### Verdict
| Area | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Channel UI (desktop + mobile) | **Works, looks right** | `client/src/views/MessengerView.vue` — sidebar + drawer + bottom nav all wired |
| Channel = chat with AI features | **Works** | `channels` getter returns chats with `mode === 'channel'`; each channel opens in `ChatView.vue` (composer, mentions, threads) |
| Threads on a message | **Works (mechanism exists)** | `$storex.chats.createNewThread` binds a child chat with `parent_id` + `message_id` |
| Unread | **Broken** | see finding 1 |
| Channel members (profiles + users) | **Not reachable** | see finding 2 |
| Team membership API | **Broken** | see finding 3 |
| Profile tool to create channels | **Exists as task creation only** | `create_task`/`project_manager` tools exist; no channel tool |
| External users | **Not started** | no guest/role concept in the chat model |
| External sync (WhatsApp/Slack) | **Not started** | no connector module in `api/codx/junior/api/` |
| Push notifications | **Not started** | no service worker / manifest in `client/public/`; no push router in the API |

### Findings that change the plan
**1. Unread has no producer and the wrong rule.** `MessengerChannelList.vue` renders `chat.unread_count` (both the expanded row and the collapsed avatar), but `client/src/store/chats.js` never sets that field on a chat — so the badge is dead. Meanwhile the only real unread rule, `client/src/utils/chatUnread.js`, requires `message.role === 'assistant'`: a human message is *by definition* never unread. For a team chat that is the wrong half of the rule.

**2. The channel has no human membership and the members panel is dead code.** `MessengerView.vue` imports `MessengerGroupInfo.vue` but **never renders it**; `showGroupInfo` only toggles a button colour, and `updateGroupMembers`/`updateGroupName`/`leaveGroup`/`membersLabel` are unreferenced. A channel carries `profiles` (AI) but no list of *people*, and `channels` returns every channel of the project to everyone — no visibility filter. That is the gap blocking both "members" and "external users".

**3. Teams is a second chat stack, and it doesn't match its own backend.** `client/src/store/teams.js` creates chats with `board: team:<id>`, keeps categories, members and DMs; the backend `api/codx/junior/model/team.py` deliberately has **no users** (a team is a roster of *profiles*), and `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py` routes by **team name** with no `/members` sub-resource. The client (`client/src/api/modules/teams.js`) addresses teams by uuid `id` and calls `POST/DELETE /api/teams/{id}/members` with `{profiles, users}`. Conclusion: `addMember`/`addProfile` in the Teams screen cannot succeed against this API. Two chat products, one of them with a broken contract — we must not build M3 on top of that ambiguity.

**4. Cost risk that is still unmeasured.** `mode: 'channel'` is declared client-side (`CHAT_MODES` in `store/chats.js`); I have not been able to *prove* from the code path whether a channel message starts an AI run. If it does, every team message pays for a model call. Task `f48e9b8d` closes this with evidence before M2.

**5. No automated tests, and the surface is only manually verifiable.** There is no messenger test suite; acceptance is a human walkthrough. Acceptable for M1, not for M5/M6 — the M0 script becomes the regression script for every demo.

**6. Cosmetic, will bite in light theme:** `MessengerView.vue` hardcodes `style="background: #111111"`, and several Tailwind classes end in a bare `hover:` with no value.

---

## 2. Scope

**In scope, increment M1 (this week):** unread badges for channels covering **human and AI** messages, mark-as-seen on open, the channel members panel rendered in both desktop and mobile layouts, mobile bottom-nav items pointing at real actions, and a written test script.
**Out of scope, M1:** external users, external sync, push notifications, profile tools for channel creation, any Teams refactor (blocked on **D1**), any change to kanban/wall unread behaviour.

---

## 3. Increment plan

Each row is a vertical slice that ships and is demoed on its own. Demo day is the last working day of the increment, 14:00.

| # | Milestone | Deliverable (what management sees) | Owner (profile) | Date | Deployable? | Demoable? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | Test baseline | Written 30-min test script + defect log; the same script reused before every demo | analyst + biblio | Tue **Nov 3** | yes (docs only) | yes (walkthrough of today's state) | **blocked** — engine produced no output, flagged on task |
| M1 | "I can follow the team from my phone" | Unread badge that counts colleagues *and* profiles, clears on open; members panel reachable on desktop and mobile | VueDeveloper | Fri **Nov 6** | yes | yes | created |
| M2 | "Talk to profiles in a channel" | `@profile` in a channel → answer in a thread; no AI spend without a mention; thread from any message | py_senior (guard) + VueDeveloper (thread UI) | **Nov 9–13** | yes | yes | prep tasks created (2) |
| M3 | "Team membership is real" | One canonical surface; add a person to a channel, they see it; Teams contract fixed or retired | py_senior + VueDeveloper | **Nov 16–20** | yes | yes | **blocked on D1** |
| M4 | "External users can join" | Invite link into one channel, scoped read/write, expiring | py_senior + devops | **Nov 23–27** | yes | yes | **blocked on D3** |
| M5 | "I get notified when away" | Browser notification on a real message with the tab closed; PWA install on the phone | web_master + py_senior | **Nov 30–Dec 4** | yes | yes | spike created (report Nov 11) |
| M6 | "Channel syncs with WhatsApp/Telegram" | One provider, real round trip both ways | py_senior | **Dec 7–11** | yes | yes | spike created (report Nov 13) |
| M7 | "A profile manages channels" | ProjectManager can create a channel, post, and turn a message into a task-thread | py_senior + analyst | **Dec 14–18** | yes | yes | backlog (needs D2 outcome) |

Sequencing rule applied: the riskiest *product* assumption (unread + members, i.e. "does this work as a team chat at all") is validated in the earliest increment, not the external integrations that look more impressive.

---

## 4. Dependencies & critical path

- **Critical path:** M1 (unread + membership UI) → M3 (one membership model, users + profiles per channel) → M4 (external users, needs a guest identity). Slip in M1 moves everything right by the same days.
- **M2 runs in parallel** with M3 (backend chat engine vs membership) — but both touch the thread contract, so `f48e9b8d` must land **before** M3 starts.
- **M5 depends on M1**: without a correct unread model we cannot say *what* to notify about.
- **M6 depends on M3/M4**: an external sender needs an identity to post as.
- **External lead time (the real long pole):** WhatsApp requires a Meta Business account, phone verification and template-message approval — typically **weeks**, and it is not in our hands. Telegram needs a bot token in minutes. Slack needs a workspace admin to approve an app.
- **Infra dependency:** browser push needs HTTPS with a valid certificate and VAPID keys in settings; the phone must be able to reach the app.

---

## 5. Risks

| # | Risk | Impact | Prob. | Mitigation | Owner | Needs decision? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Two chat surfaces (Messenger/Teams) split effort and produce two half-products | High | High | D1 this week; freeze new work on Teams until decided | Management | **Yes — D1** |
| R2 | Teams client calls non-existent endpoints → "add member" silently fails | High | Certain | Fix contract or retire Teams in M3; never demo membership from the Teams screen | py_senior | No (planned) |
| R3 | Channel message triggers a model run → token cost per team message | High | Medium | `f48e9b8d` evidence by Nov 4; guard shipped in M2 | py_senior | **Yes — D2** |
| R4 | Exposing the messenger externally without per-channel scoping = data leak | High | Medium | M4 gated on a scoped guest token + security review; no "share whole workspace" | devops | **Yes — D3** |
| R5 | WhatsApp approval lead time blows the December date | Medium | High | Telegram first (M6), start WhatsApp business verification now in parallel | Management | **Yes — D4** |
| R6 | iOS/Android push only works from an installed PWA | Medium | High | PWA install prompt inside M5; in-app toast as fallback | web_master | No (planned) |
| R7 | No automated tests; every change is manual regression | Medium | High | M0 script executed before each demo; first automated contract test in M3 | analyst | No |
| R8 | One developer, two surfaces, seven increments | Medium | Medium | Board has one owner per task; anything over one week gets re-sliced | ProjectManager | No |

---

## 6. Decisions needed from management

**D1 — Which chat surface do we build on? (decide by Wed Nov 4)**
- **A (recommended):** Messenger is the chat product; "Teams" becomes roster/membership configuration only (who is in the team, which profiles). One chat stack, one place to look for messages.
- **B:** Teams becomes canonical and Messenger is absorbed into it — larger, and the Teams ↔ backend contract is broken today, so it starts with debt.
- **C:** Both stay (Messenger = quick chat, Teams = workspace). Cheapest today, most expensive in three months — two unread models, two member lists.
- **Cost of deciding late:** M3 (Nov 16) cannot start, and everything after it moves day for day.

**D2 — AI policy inside a channel? (decide by Wed Nov 4)**
- **A (recommended):** no model call unless a profile is `@mentioned`; optional per-channel "profiles answer on their own" switch, off by default.
- **B:** profiles answer everything in their channels — maximum "alive" feeling, unbounded token cost.
- **C:** no profiles in channels at all — cheapest, but drops the "talk with profiles" part of the request.

**D3 — What exactly does "external user" mean? (decide by Fri Nov 6)**
- **A (recommended):** invite link into **one** channel, read+write, expiring, no access to the rest of the project.
- **B:** full workspace guest account — bigger security surface, needs an identity/role model we don't have.
- **Recommendation stands on A**; M4 is gated on it.

**D4 — Which external tool ships first? (decide by Fri Nov 13)**
- **A (recommended):** Telegram first (days of work, no vendor approval), WhatsApp when the Business account is verified.
- **B:** WhatsApp first — closer to your real customers, but the date is owned by Meta, not by us.
- **Action regardless of the choice:** start the WhatsApp Business verification now; it is the only item with a multi-week lead time.

**D5 — Notification policy (decide by Fri Nov 6)**
Recommended default: notify on **@mentions and direct messages** only; all channel traffic stays badge-only; no notifications 22:00–07:00. Anything broader trains people to mute the app.

---

## 7. Next demo & checkpoint

**M1 demo — Fri Nov 6, 14:00, 5 minutes, on the deployed app (not slides).**
What you will see: two sessions and a phone. A colleague posts in `#general` from a laptop; the phone shows **1** on the channel; opening it clears the badge; a profile reply also counts; the channel members panel opens on both layouts.

What the team needs to run it: a build deployed to the demo environment, **two users (or one user + one profile)**, two channels with a few messages, one phone with the app reachable over HTTPS, and the M0 script printed. If any of those are missing, the demo is postponed, not faked.

**Checkpoint for you, today (30 min, real cases):** install/open the app on the phone, create a channel, post from a second session, watch for a badge (expect **none** — that is finding 1), try to open "Members" from the mobile bottom nav (expect a dead toggle — finding 2), mention a profile in a channel and note whether it answers and whether it costs a run (finding 4). Send me the pass/fail list; it becomes the M1 acceptance evidence.

---

## 8. Demo script (M1)

1. **Laptop A** — `#general`, post "M1 demo, ready for review".
2. **Phone** — app closed to background; notification/badge expectation stated out loud. Show channel list: **1** on `#general`.
3. **Open** `#general` on the phone → message visible, badge disappears without reload. *(Acceptance: unread counts colleagues.)*
4. **Laptop B** — `@analyst summarise this channel` → answer appears; channel list shows the AI reply as unread for the other user. *(Acceptance: unread counts profiles.)*
5. **Members** — mobile bottom nav → Members → panel shows profiles **and** people on the channel. *(Acceptance: AC1 membership visible.)*
6. **Close** — "anything that could not be shown is not done": ask for accept/reject, and for the decision on D1/D2 if still open.

---

## Board state (board **Chats** › column **Team chat**)

| ID | Task | Owner profiles | Status | Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `d57b21f9` | M0 — manual test plan + defect log | analyst, biblio | **blocked** (engine produced no output; `docs/messenger/test-plan.md` not written; user help requested) | Nov 3 |
| `280d7d0c` | M1 — real unread badges for channels (human + AI) | VueDeveloper | todo (ready to run) | Nov 6 |
| `a8d16acf` | M2 prep — consolidate Messenger vs Teams (decision doc) | analyst, project | todo (ready to run) | Nov 4 |
| `f48e9b8d` | M2 prep — verify channel messages don't trigger AI runs | py_senior | todo (ready to run) | Nov 4 |
| `ae60e722` | M5 spike — push notifications (browser + mobile PWA) | web_master, py_senior | todo | report Nov 11 |
| `0dafb4e0` | M6 spike — external channel sync connector | py_senior | todo | report Nov 13 |

**Next step:** give me a go/no-go on **D1** and **D2** and I will start `a8d16acf` and `280d7d0c` immediately; `f48e9b8d` can run today regardless, because the cost answer is needed whichever surface we keep. No application code was changed in this review.

**Summary (5 lines)**

1. The team asked to turn the Messenger into a real team chat — channels + threads, humans and profiles, usable from mobile — with four acceptance criteria: chat with team members, external access, WhatsApp/Slack sync, and push notifications.
2. I reviewed `client/` and `api/` and found the UI works but the product doesn't: unread badges have no producer and only count AI messages, the channel members panel is never rendered, the Teams screen calls API endpoints that don't exist, and external sync plus push notifications are not started at all.
3. I sliced delivery into 7 weekly, independently deployable and demoable increments (M0→M7, Nov 3 to Dec 18), with M1 "follow the team from my phone" (real unread + members) as the increment that proves the product.
4. I created 6 tasks on board **Chats › Team chat** with one owner each (`d57b21f9`, `280d7d0c`, `a8d16acf`, `f48e9b8d`, `ae60e722`, `0dafb4e0`); the M0 test-plan task came back "completed" without writing its file and is flagged blocked.

#TL; DR;

1. **Review:** the Messenger exists as UI only — channel/thread plumbing works, but unread is broken (badges have no producer, and the unread rule ignores human messages), channel membership is unreachable in the UI, and the Teams screen calls API endpoints that don't exist.
2. **Greenfield:** external users, WhatsApp/Slack sync and push notifications are not started — there is no service worker, no push endpoint and no connector in the API.
